text:
alex: Customer reported sudden duplicate token charges after a timeout on our API call. They say they only clicked once but invoice shows 3x usage.
sara: Account and invoice? send me org id and example request id.
alex: org=acme-thermostats, sample request id: r-7f3c9a. Ticket id INC-7421.
diego: I pulled raw ingress logs for r-7f3c9a — looks like three inbound POSTs within 18s from same client IP, each with different ephemeral id. Gateway returned 504 on first attempt then 200s.
kiran: Did the client send an idempotency key? if not we will treat each as distinct usage.
alex: They claim they used our JS SDK which should set `Idempotency-Key`. logs show `Idempotency-Key` header present on all three but values are different: `ik-1a2`, `ik-1a2-retry`, `ik-1a2-2`.
sara: hmm SDK doc says key persisted in localStorage for 60s. Could TTL have expired after a tab crash/reconnect?
diego: Here's the relevant snippet from the edge logs:
```
[2026-01-12T15:22:03Z] r-7f3c9a ingress POST /v1/generate status=504 trace=xYz
[2026-01-12T15:22:12Z] r-7f3c9a retry POST /v1/generate status=200 trace=xYz-1
[2026-01-12T15:22:18Z] r-7f3c9a retry POST /v1/generate status=200 trace=xYz-2
headers: Idempotency-Key=ik-1a2 (first), ik-1a2-retry (second)
```
kiran: Looks like client didn't reuse exact key; inspects show SDK generates new key on network-layer reconnect if previous request timed out. TTL in localStorage=60s but our SDK rehydrates key only after promise settles — in some browsers crash path it regenerates.
billing-bot: Detected 2 additional meter events for org acme-thermostats between 2026-01-12T15:22:12Z and 15:22:18Z total_tokens=3.2k unit=token
sara: So duplicates are legitimate meter entries — gateway accepted distinct idempotency keys. We need to decide refund/credit and mitigation.
diego: Short repro I ran with patched SDK: `await client.generate(...)` then simulate network timeout and re-run — if key is different we get two charges. Repro script:
```bash
# simulate: send request, drop connection, resend new idempotency key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: ik-test-1" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' --max-time 2 || true
# resend a new request with different Idempotency-Key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: ik-test-2" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
alex: Customer wants refund for double charges for last invoice. Can billing run a ledger query to confirm 3 charge lines tied to r-7f3c9a?
sara: @billing-bot please run ledger_search(org=acme-thermostats, trace=xYz) and flag duplicates.
billing-bot: Ledger search started. Found 3 meter events with traces xYz, xYz-1, xYz-2. Suggested resolution: credit 2nd & 3rd events total 256 tokens.
kiran: Engineering fix options: 1) server-side: extend idempotency canonicalization window (consider hashing partly-equivalent keys) — risky; 2) gateway: detect repeated traces from same upstream connection within short window and dedupe by payload hash; 3) SDK: make idempotency key truly persistent across crash/reconnect and add exponential backoff rather than immediate regenerate.
eng-oncall: Priority: P2. Short-term mitigation: credit customer and enable temporary gateway dedupe for this org for 30m while we patch SDK and add telemetry.
diego: I can push a gateway rule to dedupe identical payloads for 10s window for org=acme-thermostats. Will monitor.
sara: I'll prepare a customer reply: apology, explain duplicate charges due to client retry with different idempotency keys after timeout, mention refund and next steps. Confirmed refund amount 256 tokens credited.
alex: Thank you — please add follow-up action: SDK team to increase persistence to 5 minutes for idempotency storage and document crash edgecase.
kiran: filing ENG-PR to update SDK and add e2e test for reconnect path.
eng-oncall: Closing loop: gateway rule applied at 15:30 UTC, billing credit issued, SDK PR queued. Marking as resolved for now; will reopen if more reports. :white_check_mark:
